notes: §1985:VI.6.24.3 SR2: "If a STOP RUN statement appears in a consecutive sequence of imperative statements within a sentence, it must appear as the last statement in that sequence." The statement funnel (BindStatement) asks RefusedOutOfSequence of every statement at every edition; SequenceRuleOf selects the rule for STOP RUN only (the 1985 STOP literal, which continues, is not governed, as the rule names STOP RUN), and EndsImperativeRun passes a STOP RUN that is last in its sentence or phrase or is followed by a conditional statement (IsConditional), which is the 1985 scope (the imperative run ends where a conditional statement begins, §1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1) and not the wider 2023 wording. Probed at --std 85: STOP RUN followed by DISPLAY (the witness), CONTINUE, a delimited ADD ... END-ADD or IF ... END-IF, and STOP RUN followed by a statement inside an IF phrase, an ELSE phrase and an inline PERFORM are refused with COBOL2968; STOP RUN followed by an IF, an IF ... NEXT SENTENCE, a SEARCH or an ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR without its terminator, STOP RUN ending a sentence, and STOP literal followed by DISPLAY are accepted.

next.reason: 1985: 'If a STOP RUN statement appears in a consecutive sequence of imperative statements within a sentence, it must appear as the last statement in that sequence.' §2023:14.9.42.3 SR1: 'The STOP statement shall be specified only as the last statement in any discreet block of code.' The scope words differ: 2023 drops 'consecutive sequence of imperative statements within a sentence', which the same standard keeps verbatim for GO TO (§2023:14.9.17.3 SR2), for an undefined 'discreet block of code'. Whether STOP RUN may precede a conditional statement in the same sentence (permitted by the 1985 wording) is no longer stated, so the requirement differs; a project reading (docs/CONFORMANCE.md) is not the standard.
